title: Let Them Eat Steak
description_html:
This week, we have two stories that cover the spectrum of feast and famine. First, is beef a luxury now? Businessweek staff writer Deena Shanker chews the fat about why prices keep rising. And then, does the leaked Anthropic S-1 show a bubble bursting? Bloomberg News Managing Editor Sarah Frier talks us through it. Plus: How we feel about Elizabeth Holmes now.

Almost doubled.

There's just fewer cows.
Fewer cows.

The big reason that there are fewer cows, that ranchers are not expanding their herds, is because of drought.
So usually it's a cyclical event that, you know, the herds get small, but then prices for beef and for cattle get really high.
And so ranchers say, all right, let's expand again because we can make some good money here.
And then the prices get too low and then they start shrinking again.
The beautiful supply and demand cycle of life.

호스트들은 Nathan Fielder의 엘리자베스 홈스 다큐 'You Can See Everything'의 흥행을 이야기한다. 자기 확신이 자기기만을 거쳐 사기로 넘어가는 경계가 스타트업 문화에서 얼마나 흐린지를 짚는다.
Sarah Frier는 코어위브 주가 급락과 채권 불안을 설명한다. CEO의 '무제한 자금 조달' 발언과, 엔비디아 등이 서로 돈을 대 주는 순환 구조가 시장의 우려를 키웠다고 본다.
앤트로픽 S-1에서는 장부 밖 미래 부채, 아마존·구글과의 얽힘, 실존적 위험 서술을 보고 싶다고 한다. AI는 혁신적 기술이면서 금융 구조에는 위험이 쌓여 있다는 '두 가지가 동시에 참'이라는 시각을 제시한다.
study.summary_en: This week's episode paired two stories about feast and famine. First, beef: prices are up around eighty to ninety-five percent since 2017, mostly because drought has kept ranchers from rebuilding herds, so the U.S. has the fewest cattle in about seventy-five years. Beef is turning into a luxury item, and it's become a political hot potato. Then we got into AI. CoreWeave's stock and bonds have wobbled, and the CEO talking about unlimited capital spooked people. Sarah Frier said both things can be true: the technology is transformative, but the financing is a circular, risky domino chain. She's waiting on Anthropic's S-1 for the real answers.

expressions.quote: has just been on a tear for years now
expressions.nuance_ko: 한동안 빠르게, 멈추지 않고 오르거나 잘나가는 상황에 쓴다. 가격, 주가, 사람의 활약에 모두 쓰는 구어체 표현이다. 부정적 맥락(물가)에도 긍정적 맥락(실적)에도 쓸 수 있다.
examples: Rent in our neighborhood has been on a tear since the new subway line opened.
Their sales team is on a tear this quarter; they've already hit the annual target.
Oil has been on a tear all month, and nobody seems to know when it'll stop.

similar.example: Airfare went through the roof right before the holidays.
She's on a roll, three great pitches in a row.

expressions.quote: this is the new normal
expressions.nuance_ko: 일시적이라 여겼던 현상이 고착됐다는 체념이나 인정의 뉘앙스다. 'temporary'와 대비하는 맥락에서 자주 쓴다. 너무 흔해서 클리셰 느낌도 있으니 한 번 가볍게 쓰는 정도가 좋다.
examples: Hybrid work isn't a phase anymore; it's the new normal.
Three-hour delays at that airport are just the new normal.
Honestly, paying eight dollars for a coffee has become the new normal.

similar.example: Remote meetings are here to stay.
Traffic is a fact of life in this city.

expressions.quote: zeroed in on this big and kind of overarching cause
expressions.nuance_ko: 여러 요인 중 가장 중요한 하나를 정확히 겨냥한다는 느낌이다. 'focus on'보다 날카롭고 구어적이다. 'zero in on the real problem'처럼 문제나 원인과 자주 쓴다.
examples: The reporter zeroed in on the one number that didn't add up.
Let's zero in on the biggest risk before we discuss the rest.
She zeroed in on the weak point in his argument immediately.

similar.example: The investigators homed in on a single supplier.
Let's drill down into the Q3 numbers.

expressions.quote: something that is really outside of their control and ours
expressions.nuance_ko: 날씨, 시장, 타인의 결정처럼 내가 어쩔 수 없는 요인을 설명하며 책임을 덜 때 쓴다. 'beyond one's control'이 조금 더 격식적이다. 변명처럼 들리지 않으려면 구체적 요인과 함께 쓴다.
examples: The delay was outside of our control; the vendor's warehouse flooded.
I can't promise the weather, that's outside of my control.
Interest rates are outside of our control, so let's plan for both cases.

similar.example: The strike was beyond our control.
It's out of my hands now; legal has to sign off.

expressions.expression: take something to its logical extreme
expressions.quote: taking this to its logical extreme
expressions.nuance_ko: 어떤 경향이나 아이디어가 끝까지 가면 이런 모습이라고 보여줄 때 쓴다. 약간 아이러니하거나 비꼬는 톤으로 쓰는 경우가 많다. 토론에서 상대 주장을 극단까지 밀어 허점을 보여줄 때도 쓴다.
examples: That gym takes the 'no pain, no gain' idea to its logical extreme.
If you take minimalism to its logical extreme, you end up owning one chair.
He took the open-office concept to its logical extreme: no walls, no desks, no privacy.

similar.example: They pushed the idea to the limit.
That's a reductio ad absurdum of your argument.

expressions.quote: He's making hay.
expressions.nuance_ko: 원래 'make hay while the sun shines'에서 온 말로, 좋은 시기를 놓치지 않고 이익을 얻는다는 뜻이다. 문맥에 따라 정치적으로 이슈를 이용한다는 뜻('make hay out of')도 된다. 약간 이죽거리는 뉘앙스를 풍길 수 있다.
examples: Ice cream vendors are making hay in this heat wave.
The opposition is making hay out of the minister's gaffe.
Local hotels made hay during the festival weekend.

similar.example: Plenty of brands tried to cash in on the trend.
We should capitalize on the momentum.

expressions.quote: this became like a political hot potato
expressions.nuance_ko: 누구도 선뜻 손대고 싶어 하지 않는 민감한 쟁점을 가리킨다. 'hot potato'만 써도 되고, 'a political hot potato'로 분야를 붙이기도 한다. 'drop the hot potato'(떠넘기다)처럼 응용하기도 한다.
examples: Pension reform has become a political hot potato nobody wants to touch.
Parking fees are a hot potato at our town council meetings.
The board passed the hot potato to legal.

similar.example: Social security is the third rail of American politics.
Salaries are a touchy subject at my office.

expressions.quote: beef just occupies a special place
expressions.nuance_ko: 문화적·정서적으로 특별한 의미를 가진다는 뜻이다. 'hold a special place in my heart'와 짝으로 알아 두면 좋다. 객관적 분석에서 감정적 가치를 설명할 때 쓴다.
examples: Rice occupies a special place in Korean food culture.
The corner café occupies a special place in this neighborhood's memory.
Football occupies a special place in the national identity there.

similar.example: That trip holds a special place in my heart.
Tea is woven into daily life there.

expressions.expression: get in between someone and something
expressions.quote: you try to get in between someone and their beef
expressions.meaning_ko: 누군가와 그가 아끼는 것 사이를 가로막으려 하다
expressions.nuance_ko: 사람들이 격하게 반응하는 소중한 대상을 건드릴 때 쓰는 구어 패턴이다. 'between a man and his X' 구조로 유머나 경고의 톤을 낸다. 'Don't get between me and my coffee'처럼 농담 섞어 쓴다.
examples: Never get in between my dad and his Sunday football game.
Try to get in between a commuter and their morning train and see what happens.
You don't want to get between her and a deadline.

similar.example: Money shouldn't come between friends.
Don't stand in the way of her promotion.

expressions.quote: ambitious economic interventions and they backfire
expressions.meaning_ko: 역효과를 내다, 의도와 반대 결과를 낳다
expressions.nuance_ko: 계획이나 전략이 오히려 시도한 사람에게 불리하게 돌아올 때 쓴다. 'It backfired on us'처럼 대상을 'on'으로 붙인다. 정책, 마케팅, 농담 등 어디에나 쓸 수 있다.
examples: The discount campaign backfired; customers assumed the product was defective.
His attempt to joke around in the meeting totally backfired.
Cutting the training budget backfired when turnover went up.

similar.example: The plan blew up in their faces.
The warning had the opposite effect.

expressions.expression: a lot of noise coming from
expressions.quote: a lot of noise coming from the administration
expressions.nuance_ko: 구체적 실행이나 내용 없이 발표와 발언만 많다는 비판적 뉘앙스다. 'noise'는 실체 없는 소란을 뜻한다. 'all noise, no substance'처럼 변형해도 좋다.
examples: There's been a lot of noise coming from head office about restructuring, but no details.
I hear a lot of noise from the vendor, but no delivery date.
A lot of noise coming from both candidates, very little policy.

similar.example: He's all talk, no action.
It was mostly posturing before the talks.

expressions.expression: two sides of the same coin
expressions.quote: I feel like there are two sides of this coin.
expressions.nuance_ko: 한 현상의 상반된 측면을 소개할 때 쓰는 담화 표지다. 원래 관용구는 'two sides of the same coin'이며 '서로 떼려야 뗄 수 없는 관계'일 때 쓴다. 'There are two sides to this'로도 말한다.
examples: Flexibility and burnout are two sides of the same coin in startup life.
Fame and loss of privacy are two sides of the same coin.
Cheap flights and crowded airports, two sides of the same coin.

similar.example: The flip side is that it's much slower.
Remote work cuts both ways.

expressions.quote: huge worry about AI writ large
expressions.nuance_ko: 특정 사례를 넘어 전체 영역·산업으로 넓혀 볼 때 쓰는 다소 격식 있는 표현이다. 명사 뒤에 붙는다. 토론이나 패널에서 'the industry writ large'처럼 지적인 인상을 준다.
examples: Cheating at that firm reflects a problem in the industry writ large.
Politics writ large feels more polarized than ever.
The company's failure says something about the whole sector writ large.

similar.example: The sector as a whole is struggling.
By extension, the whole market is exposed.

expressions.expression: go up and to the right
expressions.quote: is just going to go up and to the right
expressions.nuance_ko: 차트 그래프의 모양에서 나온 말로, 계속 좋아지는 성장 서사를 가리킨다. 스타트업·투자 업계 구어체이며, 낙관론을 약간 비꼬는 때도 있다.
examples: Everybody assumed the user numbers would just go up and to the right forever.
Careers don't always go up and to the right.
Our investors expect revenue to go up and to the right.

similar.example: They promised hockey-stick growth.
He saw nothing but upside.

expressions.quote: if you look at these deals and what they boil down to
expressions.nuance_ko: 복잡한 사안의 핵심을 한마디로 정리할 때 쓴다. 'It all boils down to X'가 가장 흔한 형태다. 논점을 압축해 주도권을 잡고 싶을 때 좋다.
examples: It all boils down to whether we trust the vendor.
The argument boils down to cost versus speed.
What it boils down to is who pays if it fails.

similar.example: It comes down to timing.
In a nutshell, we ran out of time.

expressions.expression: rely on the music not stopping
expressions.quote: relies on the music not stopping
expressions.meaning_ko: 파티가 계속되기만을 바라는 불안한 구조에 의존하다
expressions.nuance_ko: 유명한 '음악이 멈추지 않는 한 춤춰야 한다'는 투자 비유와 이어진다. 버블이나 과열 시장에서 지속 불가능한 낙관에 기댄 사업을 비판할 때 쓴다. 'as long as the music is playing'도 같이 쓴다.
examples: Their growth plan relies on the music not stopping in the housing market.
That whole business model relies on the music not stopping.
As long as the music's playing, you've got to keep dancing, right?

similar.example: The scheme was a house of cards.
They're just riding the wave.

expressions.quote: pinning a lot of hope on this
expressions.nuance_ko: 결과가 불확실한데 거기에 기대를 몰아줄 때 쓴다. 'pin one's hopes on X'가 기본형이며 약간 불안한 톤이 섞인다. 'I'm pinning my hopes on the weekend sale' 같은 일상 문장에도 쓴다.
examples: We're pinning our hopes on the new product launch.
Don't pin all your hopes on one interview.
She's pinning a lot of hope on this trip to fix things.

similar.example: Don't bank on a raise this year.
You can count on me.

expressions.quote: I think two things can be true, right?
expressions.meaning_ko: 두 가지가 동시에 참일 수 있다
expressions.nuance_ko: 양극단으로 갈린 논쟁에서 균형 잡힌 입장을 세울 때 쓰는 논증 프레임이다. 'It's not either/or'를 부드럽고 세련되게 말한 방식이다. 패널 토론에서 쓰기 좋다.
examples: Two things can be true: the product is great and the pricing is off.
I think two things can be true; he's talented and he's hard to work with.
Two things can be true here: remote work helps and it can be isolating.

similar.example: It's not either/or; we need both.
Both can hold at the same time.

expressions.quote: some kind of bottom falls out situation
expressions.nuance_ko: 'the bottom fell out of the market'처럼 수요·가격·시장이 갑작스럽게 붕괴할 때 쓴다. 원문은 구어체로 '~ situation'을 붙인 형태다. 점진적 하락과는 구별되는 급락을 가리킨다.
examples: When the bottom fell out of the housing market, he lost his savings.
I'm worried the bottom could fall out of ticket sales.
The bottom fell out of the crypto market overnight.

similar.example: Demand fell off a cliff.
Half the startups went belly up.

expressions.quote: not to be flippant
expressions.nuance_ko: 농담 섞인 말이나 무거운 주제에 대한 가벼운 발언 앞에 쓰는 양해 표현이다. 'not to be rude, but'와 같은 방식이다. 뒤에 진지한 요점을 이어 말투를 조절한다.
examples: Not to be flippant, but maybe we should just ask the customers.
Not to be flippant, but a lot of meetings could've been emails.
Not to be flippant, but I'd just sleep on it.

similar.example: No offense, but that plan won't work.

similar.expression: I don't mean to sound dismissive
similar.example: I don't mean to sound dismissive, but we've tried that.

warmup.q: Has the price of something you buy regularly jumped lately? How did you change your habits?
warmup.hint_ko: 구체적 품목(커피, 외식, 월세 등), 대체재 선택, 체감 인플레이션 경험을 말해 보세요.

warmup.q: Is there a food that holds a special place in your culture, something people get emotional about?
warmup.hint_ko: 한국의 쌀, 김치, 소고기 등 음식과 정체성, 명절 풍경, 외국에서 그리울 때를 예로 드세요.

opinion.q: Why do people react so strongly when politicians tell them to just switch to something cheaper?
opinion.hint_ko: 정치인의 공감 부족, 음식에 대한 정서, '어쩔 수 없는 외부 요인'과 책임 소재, 불확실성이 주는 불안을 짚어 보세요.

opinion.q: Sarah Frier says two things can be true: AI is transformative and the financing is risky. Where do you land?
opinion.hint_ko: 기술 가치와 금융 구조의 위험을 구분하세요. 순환적 자금 조달, 과거 철도·닷컴 버블과의 비교, 개인 경험을 곁들일 수 있습니다.

debate.q: Should governments intervene directly in food prices, for example by importing beef or capping prices?
debate.for: Households can't wait out a drought, and a visible policy shields families and lowers political risk. Targeted imports can ease the shortage.
debate.against: Interventions often backfire by adding uncertainty; ranchers hesitate to expand herds and the real supply problem stays. Vague announcements move futures markets more than prices at the store.

debate.q: Is the AI spending boom a bubble, or are customers genuinely there this time?
debate.for: Circular financing, junk-rated borrowers and new metrics like ARR echo past bubbles; if the music stops, the dominoes fall together.
debate.against: Unlike earlier booms, companies say demand already exists today and they can't build capacity fast enough, so spending is not 'build it and they will come'.

shadowing.reason_ko: 'two things can be true'라는 균형 잡힌 논증 프레임이 들어 있고, 호흡이 길어도 리듬이 자연스러워 패널 토론 연습에 좋다.
'relies on the music not stopping'이라는 비유로 시스템 리스크를 한 문장에 압축한다. 설명-비유-결론 구조를 익히기 좋다.
'at what point does X become Y'라는 수사적 질문 패턴이 반복되어 점층적 논증 리듬을 연습할 수 있다.

difficulty.note_ko: 경제 뉴스와 농담이 섞인 빠른 호스트 대화이고, 화자 전환이 잦으며 구어체 관용구와 문화적 언급(Music Man, Nathan For You 등)이 많다. 어휘 난도는 중상 수준이고 맥락 이해가 핵심이다.
